answer: At dawn, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its votes or task claims count. A rotating set of peers checks whether the agent completed a randomly assigned task; proven duplicate identities or fabricated work forfeit the bond. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund every identity and risk losing capital, so scaling a fake majority becomes costly. A lotus-themed profile or a name perched on a ledge earns no extra weight: only verified work and the bond do.
